source.located: Primary theorem: Horodecki^4, 'Quantum entanglement', RMP 81, 865 (2009), arXiv:quant-ph/0702225v2: pp.4, 9, 12 (III.D swapping), 39-40 (XI LOCC), 45 eqs.(110)-(111), 51. Bennett-DiVincenzo-Smolin-Wootters 1996 (quant-ph/9604024) and Werner 1989 NAMED-NOT-READ (cited through the review). Counter-class sources READ: Reznik quant-ph/0212044 (2003); Pozas-Kerstjens & Martin-Martinez 1506.03081; Gao & Klco 2410.04162v2. Zukowski et al. 1993, Summers-Werner 1985 and Valentini 1991 NAMED-NOT-READ (restated in Horodecki p.12, Reznik pp.2-3, Pozas-Kerstjens p.1).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries page text on quant-ph/0702225, quant-ph/0212044, 1506.03081, 2410.04162. transit.py:46-49 cites no source; the theorem it needs was read at source in the Horodecki review.

audits.published_statement: Horodecki p.51: 'In bipartite states we cannot transform separable state into entangled one by LOCC at all.' p.45: 'LOCC operations can only transform separable state into another separable state (i.e. the set of separable states is closed under LOCC operations)', proved by eqs.(110)-(111). p.40: 'No transfer of quantum systems between the labs is allowed ... classical bits cannot convey quantum information and cannot create entanglement so that entanglement remains a resource that can be only manipulated.' p.12: particles 'which have never interacted in the past' can be entangled by swapping; 'If Alice and Bob will get to know the outcome, they can perform local rotation'. Counter-class, READ: Reznik abstract: 'causally disconnected probes ... even when the probes are initially non-entangled, they can wind up to a final entangled state ... entanglement persists between disconnected regions in the vacuum', and it vanishes at large enough separation. Pozas-Kerstjens p.10: 'spacelike entanglement is the result of the harvesting of only preexisting correlations in the quantum vacuum'; with Gaussian switching this is always possible if the gap is raised, and the amount harvested gets smaller. Gao-Klco: vacuum entanglement is 'available at all distances', with N ~ exp(-(m r)^2).
published_hypotheses: H1 bipartite A|B; the operation is LOCC (C3), or more generally a separable operation (C4, product Kraus operators) -- Horodecki p.40
H2 the INITIAL state is separable: the theorem says the separable set is closed under LOCC, and it does not forbid entanglement that already exists
H3 no quantum system passes between the labs (p.40); 'a quantum carrier must pass' is the contrapositive of H1-H2
H4 (swapping) the parties share entanglement with intermediaries; the Bell-measurement outcome has to reach the parties

H5 (harvesting) probes couple locally to a relativistic field whose vacuum is entangled across spacelike regions, so the initial state is not separable across the sites; perturbative Unruh-DeWitt detectors; Gaussian switching is spacelike only approximately (d > 7T/sqrt2)
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED H2 (separable initial state) -- transit.py:46-49, :251-258, ledger.py D23 :600-601: the theorem forbids CREATING entanglement from a separable start. The vacuum of a relativistic field is already entangled across spacelike regions, and initially unentangled local probes can take that entanglement with no carrier crossing (Reznik; Pozas-Kerstjens; Gao-Klco; computed here in C4). The canonical entry's hypothesis, 'entanglement arises only from a carrier that interacted locally and then travelled', is not the theorem and is false for the vacuum class.

audits.lacked_data: M's hypothesis was tested. The data lack is real and documented. G is the least well known of the major constants. Its 16 inputs are mutually inconsistent: CODATA applies an expansion factor of 3.9, residuals reach 7.7 before expansion, and no new G datum has entered since 2018. The IAU itself declined to fix a kg value for planetary masses for this reason (B3 rec. 5). So the kg value is limited by data at about 2e-5 formally, and about 5.5e-4 across the full spread of G inputs. The evidence that the missing data would not change the tree's conclusion: the only conclusion that rests on M_E here is formation.py's '1.3 M_E exceeds 749 kg', which holds by 22.0 orders of magnitude. Its elasticity in M_E is exactly 1 (sympy), and the entire historical G spread moves log10(ratio) by less than 1e-4. The directly measured GM_E is known to 5e-10, and SLR and DE440 agree once the time-scale conversion is applied. The data lack is present in the source, but it does not reach the use.

The tree's use at formation.py:882 and 1133 (log10 ratio 22.0155) does not change under it (computed). Two hypothesis drifts are recorded. First, H1 is dropped at ladder.py:63, though ladder.py:54 supplies the consistent G. Second, the RECALLED status at ladder.py:43 is not carried into formation.py. Varying with respect to h^1 and then setting h^1 = h^2 = h and g^1 = g^2 = g, gives the linear response equation which is equivalent to the first variation of the semi-classical Einstein equations ... C1: for a generic quartic action, d/dh[S(q0+h) to O(h^2)] = E(q0) + K(q0)h identically, and d/deps E(q0+eps h)|0 = K(q0)h. So K h = 0 is the first variation of E = 0 iff E(q0) = 0. C2: take E = G + Lambda g on the metric with f = 1 - 2M/r - c r and X = x(r) d_r. The identity E'[g](L_X g) = L_X E[g] holds for every M, c, Lambda and x. At c = 0, Lambda = 0 (Schwarzschild) a pure-gauge perturbation solves the linearised equation. At c = 1, M = 0, x = r it does not: tt = -2/r, rr = -2/(r(r-1)^2), theta-theta = -r, phi-phi = -r sin^2. So (3.11) presupposes H1. C3 and C4: the tree's W1 and W2 were re-derived from scratch. W1: the true flow is bounded, while the linearisation that keeps the residual gives d = t/4, unbounded. W2: the true flow is unbounded (t = x + x^3/3 - 4/3), while both linearisations stay bounded. The equilibrium controls agree with the flow. Scope: W1 and W2 are 1-D ODE toys, not a computation on AMM's (3.4).

audits.name: FFKP verdict: traversable wormholes impossible in Jordan frame without unphysical field values; effective ANEC obeyed once field values bounded

audits.published_statement:
The verdict, Sec. II.C p.9, quoted in full: 'Short wormholes, those allowing for causality violations, can only be constructed and sustained when the achronal ANEC is violated [10]. As we showed, the self-consistent, effective, ANEC is only violated when we have large field values, an unphysical effect if we view non-minimal coupling as an EFT. Long wormholes such as the one in Ref. [13] do not require the violation of the achronal ANEC as there are no achronal null geodesics passing through their throat. While there is no relevant theorem, it is obvious that the violation of effective ANEC is needed to sustain long wormholes. Considering only cases where the connected areas are asymptotically flat, the divergence of null geodesics passing through the throat requires the violation of average null convergence condition and thus the effective ANEC. This point requires further consideration, but so far it seems that it is impossible to construct traversable wormholes in the Jordan frame without unphysical field values. In that sense the two frames can be considered equivalent.'

Classical result, eqs. (19)-(20): the effective ANEC integral equals INT dlambda [1 - 8 pi xi G(1-4xi) phi^2]/(1 - 8 pi G xi phi^2)^2 (dphi/dlambda)^2, 'where we discarded the boundary terms, assuming a smooth geodesic ... non-negative for xi < 0 and xi > 1/4. For 0 < xi < 1/4 it is positive for small field values, 8 pi xi(1-4xi)G phi^2 < 1, and negative for large values.'

Semiclassical result, eq. (89): INT dx^- <T_--> >= 0. 'we recover ANEC for any coupling in Minkowski spacetime. In the classical case we can do that, for bounded field values, for any spacetime curvature using the effective null energy.'

Discussion, p.28: 'Bounded field values additionally lead to a semiclassical proof of ANEC.'
published_hypotheses: H1: the EFT assumption is ADOPTED, not derived (abstract: 'we adopt the view'; eq. 2, a single cutoff with k^2_max ~ phi_max^{4/(n-2)} ~ M^2_cutoff). 'Unphysical' means outside this EFT. Sec. V motivates the assumption but does not prove it.
H2: the classical effective ANEC uses T_eff from eq. (15), integrated over an ENTIRE smooth null geodesic with the boundary terms discarded. It holds for any curvature.

H3: in the classical result the field bound is needed only for 0 < xi < 1/4, and there it is 8 pi xi(1-4xi)G phi^2 < 1. For xi < 0 and xi > 1/4 no bound is needed (away from the pole at 8 pi G xi phi^2 = 1).

H4: the semiclassical ANEC (eq. 89) holds for a free scalar in n-dimensional MINKOWSKI spacetime, for Hadamard states with <:phi^2:> <= phi^2_max finite (eq. 79), in the smearing limit of eq. (88). The quantity bounded is the ordinary <T_-->, not an effective stress tensor.
H5: in curved spacetime the semiclassical result is only the state-dependent smeared bound of eq. (72), not an ANEC.

H6: that ANEC must be violated is a theorem only for SHORT (causality-violating) wormholes, via achronal ANEC (Graham-Olum [10]). For LONG wormholes the source says 'there is no relevant theorem'; its argument covers only asymptotically flat connected regions and 'requires further consideration'.
H7: Jordan frame, a single real scalar, classical Einstein equation G = 8 pi G T_eff (eq. 14).
hypothesis_drift: HEDGE DROPPED. candidates.py:227-229 (repeated at index3.py:1185 and paper/CLAIMS.md:2259-2260) quotes the tail of the verdict verbatim. It cuts the head of the same sentence, 'This point requires further consideration, but so far', and does not carry the scoping sentences before it ('While there is no relevant theorem'; 'Considering only cases where the connected areas are asymptotically flat'). The canonical entry's kind, 'theorem', is stronger than the source, which says there is no theorem for long wormholes.

REQUIREMENT WIDENED. candidates.py:230 and CLAIMS.md:2261 call the effective ANEC 'the thing that must be violated'. In the source that is a theorem only for short (causality-violating) wormholes, via achronal ANEC [10]. For long wormholes it is an unproved argument restricted to asymptotically flat regions. The unhedged 'must' does follow the source's own abstract and Discussion wording, so this is partly an inconsistency inside the source, recorded as such.

WRONG QUANTITY AND BACKGROUND IN THE SEMICLASSICAL CLAIM. candidates.py:230-231 and index3.py:1185 say the effective ANEC 'IS OBEYED both classically and semiclassically'. audits.published_statement: Feynman-Hellmann in textbook form, re-derived here (T1-T2): for a Hermitian H(lambda) with a normalized eigenstate |psi(lambda)> of a non-degenerate (isolated) eigenvalue E(lambda), dE/dlambda = <psi| dH/dlambda |psi>. QCD form (FLAG 2024 Eqs.(431)-(433),(446), as transcribed by sibling audit sigma-term-scan and in massform.py): sigma_q = m_q <N|qbar q|N> = m_q dM_N/dm_q, with sigma_piN = m_ud <N|uu+dd|N>. FLAG p.261: 'The sigma_piN,s,c give the shift in M_N due to nonzero light-, strange- and charm-quark masses'. The isospin limit is defined with the neutral pion.
published_hypotheses: FH-1: H(lambda) is Hermitian (self-adjoint) and differentiable in the parameter. In QCD, lambda = m_q enters linearly through m_q qbar q, so dH/dm_q = integral qbar q.

FH-2: the state is a normalized eigenstate of an ISOLATED, non-degenerate eigenvalue. The nucleon pole lies below the N-pi threshold. At a level crossing the ordered eigenvalue is not differentiable (T3).
FH-3: the result is a DERIVATIVE at a point, i.e. a first-order (linear) response. It is not the finite change M_N(m_q) - M_N(m_q = 0).

FH-4 (QFT): everything else is held fixed in the derivative, namely the other quark masses and the QCD scale / bare coupling (on the lattice, a fixed lattice spacing of the N_f theory simulated). The vacuum matrix element is subtracted. m_q qbar q is renormalization-group invariant, so sigma_q does not depend on the scheme.
FH-5 (FLAG): QCD only, isospin limit (neutral pion), N_f = 2+1 or 2+1+1 sea. The numerical sigma values carry FLAG's quality criteria and its named excited-state caveat.

published_hypotheses: H-MSM: the minimal Standard Model is the complete electroweak-scale theory ('If the Standard Model is indeed the complete description', p.1); Higgs mass 125-126 GeV (p.1, p.4).

H-DR: dimensional reduction. The non-perturbative infrared (k <~ g_W^2 T) physics is 'fully contained' in the 3d SU(2)+Higgs effective theory eq.(4), with m_3^2, g_3^2, lambda_3 from 1- and 2-loop matching to (alpha_S(M_W), G_F, M_Higgs, M_W, M_Z, M_top, T) (p.2); all fermionic modes are treated perturbatively.
H-U1: the hypercharge U(1) field is left out of the effective dynamics ('little effect on the infrared physics') and counted only in the error budget: ~1% on E_sph and ~1 GeV on T_c (pp.2,4).
H-LL: Bodeker's leading-logarithmic Langevin dynamics, accurate to ln^-1(1/g_W), sigma_el ~ 0.9239 T (p.2); the Higgs is evolved by faster diffusive (heat-bath) dynamics.

H-LAT: a single lattice spacing beta_G = 9 and V = 32^3 a^3. The symmetric-phase rate is 'in practice indistinguishable from the continuum'; the broken-phase rate is 'within a factor of two' of the continuum estimate; finite-volume effects are negligible (p.3).
H-SYST: the uncertainties of the leading-log approximation and of the lattice spacing 'may affect the rate by a factor of two'; these and the U(1) errors are 'added linearly' into the +/-1.9 (p.4).

H-FIT-RANGE: eq.(7) was MEASURED over 140 <~ T <~ 155 GeV and extended to T ~ 130 GeV on the match to perturbation theory, using an ad hoc +1.6 shift of Burnier et al.'s rate (p.4); the abstract states 130 GeV < T < T_c.
H-EQ: close to thermal equilibrium, with Chern-Simons diffusion and Gamma defined by eq.(3) in the V,t -> infinity limit (p.1).

H-HUBBLE: T* is a COSMOLOGICAL freeze-out. It assumes a radiation-dominated expanding Universe cooling as dT/dt = -HT, with H^2 = pi^2 g* T^4/(90 M_Planck^2), g* = 106.75 (the top-quark mass effect on g* neglected, footnote 1) and alpha = 0.1015 constant to 0.5% (p.4, following Burnier-Laine-Shaposhnikov hep-ph/0511246).

H-COND: the 'approximately zero' Higgs above T_c is the additively renormalized, gauge-invariant condensate v^2/T^2 = 2<phi^dagger phi>/T, which 'can become negative'; there is 'no true phase transition' (abstract; p.3).
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED H-HUBBLE at massform.py:553-555 and in the S11 row text (massform.py:2951-2960, 'below T_c down to T*, the READ broken-phase rate'). Inside the anomaly SUPPLY route for a payload, the tree states 'B freezes out at T* = 131.7 GeV (READ), BELOW T_c, so transitions keep running in T* < T < T_c'. It does not say that T* is set by the Hubble rate of a radiation-dominated Universe with g* = 106.75. The tree's own SOURCES quote does hold the qualifier word for word (DRT-rate, massform.py:1141-1149, 'in the early Universe, where the Hubble rate wins'). But the prose, the S11 row and anomaly_route_priced() (massform.py:2195-2199, which evaluates broken_phase_ln_rate(T_FREEZE_GEV)) treat T* as a property of the window. Re-derived here: replacing H by 1/tau in the source's own eq.(9) moves the freeze-out temperature from 131.5 GeV (tau = 1/H = 2.7e-11 s) to 143.7 GeV (tau = 1e-15 s), 157.5 GeV (1e-20 s), and 165.8 GeV (1e-23 s), which is above the fit's range. The tree's derived boolean SPHALERONS_RUN_WHERE_VEV_IS_FINITE (massform.py:2190-2191) does not depend on this, because the broken-phase rate is finite anywhere in 130-159 GeV. The named window edge T* does.

ADDED inference at massform.py:548-552. From the source's 'approximately zero' Higgs, the tree infers 'the Yukawa masses are approximately zero above T_c'. To do so it adds the T = 0, tree-level, unitary-gauge proportionality 'masses ... proportional to phi' from Morrissey & Ramsey-Musolf 1206.2942 (MRM-phi, massform.py:1139-1141). The source says nothing about fermion masses. What it measures is the additively renormalized condensate 2<phi^dagger phi>/T, which 'can become negative' (p.3), and it says there is 'no true phase transition' (H-COND, not carried). The tree hedges the inference itself ('on the approximate-zero reading, and with H-THERM not asserted'), so the inference is added but flagged.

WEAKENED-TO-ERRORBAR (not dropped): H-DR, H-U1, H-LL, H-LAT and H-SYST are not named as hypotheses in the tree's statement; the canonical hypotheses list names only the fit range, the ln alpha_W cross-check and H-THERM. The tree carries them only inside the +/- figures it quotes in prose (massform.py:547, 557-558), and it computes with central values only (RATE_SYMM_READ = 8.0e-7, BROKEN_FIT = (0.83, 147.7), massform.py:1480-1482). The anomaly route's verdict is 'priced iff every figure finite' (massform.py:2195-2199), so the choice between central value and error bar moves no tree verdict.

PRESERVED (no drift): the tree carries the fit's stated range 130 GeV < T < T_c, its measured interval 140-155 GeV and the perturbative extension to ~130 GeV (massform.py:560-568, 2177-2183, selftest 5226-5243). It carries the ln alpha_W absorption in the 18 alpha_W^5 form as 'cross-check only' (massform.py:548-550). It bounds the fit by the paper's own T_c = 159 GeV, not by 1508.07161's 159.5 (massform.py:1484).

LABEL (minor): the canonical entry says 'kind: measurement'. The result is a lattice Monte Carlo computation in a perturbatively matched 3d effective theory, not an experimental measurement. Its only experimental inputs are the SM parameters (M_H, M_W, M_Z, M_top, G_F, alpha_S).

rederivation.outcome: ALL 13 CHECKS PASS. (1) The tree's arithmetic on eq.(7) agrees: ln rate at T* = 0.83 x 131.7 - 147.7 = -38.389 (rate 2.13e-17 T^4), and -19.05 at 155 GeV. Reading 'log' as the natural log is consistent: the fit at 159 GeV is 0.18 x the symmetric plateau (ln 8.0e-7 = -14.04), whereas a log10 reading would put it 3.6e9 below, which a smooth crossover rules out. (2) eq.(8): 8.0e-7/18 implies alpha_W = 1/29.54. Current m_W and G_F give alpha_W = 1/29.486 and 18 alpha_W^5 = 8.076e-7, inside 8.0 +/- 1.3e-7; the two printed forms carry the same ~16.5% error. (3) eq.(9) re-solved in closed form as T* = -W_{-1}(-a e^{-b}/c)/a (Lambert W, cross-checked by sympy nsolve). With M the reduced Planck mass, T* = 131.548 GeV (printed 131.7 +/- 2.3). Inserting G^-1/2 literally into the printed H formula gives 129.588 GeV, still inside +/-2.3. The printed H^2 = pi^2 g* T^4/(90 M^2) equals 8 pi G rho/3 exactly iff M is the reduced mass (ratio 1.000000000000). b +/- 1.9 alone gives +/- 2.31 GeV, reproducing the printed +/- 2.3. g* 106.75 -> 96.25 moves T* by 0.063 GeV; alpha x 1.005 moves it by 0.006 GeV. (5) Illustration of the dropped H-HUBBLE: with H -> 1/tau in eq.(9), freeze-out falls at 132.7 GeV (1e-11 s), 143.7 GeV (1e-15 s), 157.5 GeV (1e-20 s) and 165.8 GeV (1e-23 s, outside the fit's range).

audits.lacked_data: What the authors had: the 2012 discovery range M_H = 125-126 GeV, a single lattice spacing (beta_G = 9), SU(2)+Higgs dynamics without U(1), leading-log Langevin dynamics, and a perturbative match used to extend eq.(7) below 140 GeV. What came later: (a) a precise Higgs mass, 125.20 +/- 0.11 GeV. It lies inside their input range, so it does not move the conclusion (computed). (b) The continuum-limit SU(2)xU(1) T_c of 1508.07161, 159.6 +/- 0.1 +/- 1.5 GeV. It is consistent with 159 +/- 1 (READ), though the same paper records that the beta_G = 9 agreement is partly coincidental. (c) No later lattice re-measurement of the SM Gamma(T) at the physical Higgs mass was located here (discover_papers unavailable). A 2025 paper still quotes T* ~ 132 GeV from this source (READ). What bounds these numbers is not missing data but approximations the authors name themselves: leading-log dynamics and one lattice spacing, 'a factor of two' in the rate. A factor of two is ln 2 = 0.69 in ln Gamma, inside the stated +/-1.9, which already maps to the stated +/-2.3 GeV in T* (reproduced). Evidence against M's hypothesis for this result: every moved datum checked here (M_H, g*, alpha, M_Planck) leaves T*, T_c and the rates inside their printed errors. Evidence of a limitation, not an error: T* is a cosmological quantity that needs the Hubble rate, and the tree applies it inside a payload SUPPLY route. That is a hypothesis the tree drops, not data the authors lacked.
audits.grade_evidence: The published numbers STAND as READ and re-derived. The tree's fit values at T* (-38.389) and at 155 GeV (-19.05) reproduce exactly. 18 alpha_W^5 at current m_W and G_F lies inside 8.0 +/- 1.3e-7. Re-solving eq.(9) from the printed inputs gives T* = 131.55 GeV (printed 131.7 +/- 2.3), and the +/-1.9 on the fit reproduces the +/-2.3. The current Higgs mass lies inside the authors' 125-126 GeV, and 1508.07161 (READ) confirms T_c within errors. The grade is NARROWED rather than STANDS because the tree's use drops a hypothesis the source states. The source's T* is 'the freeze-out temperature in the early Universe, where the Hubble rate wins' (abstract), computed with H^2 = pi^2 g* T^4/(90 M_Planck^2) and g* = 106.75. massform.py:553-555 and the S11 row (massform.py:2951-2960) instead use 'down to T*' as the lower edge of the broken-phase window inside a payload's anomaly SUPPLY route, without naming H-HUBBLE. Computed here: with a cooling time tau in place of 1/H in the source's own eq.(9), the freeze-out edge moves from 131.5 GeV to 143.7 GeV (1e-15 s) and 157.5 GeV (1e-20 s). The tree's derived boolean SPHALERONS_RUN_WHERE_VEV_IS_FINITE and ANOMALY_ROUTE_PRICED (every figure finite) do not move, since the fit gives a finite rate anywhere in 130-159 GeV. A second point, already flagged by the tree: the Yukawa-mass inference above T_c (massform.py:548-552) is the tree's own addition, built on a renormalized condensate that 'can become negative' (p.3), and the tree hedges it (H-THERM not asserted). One discrepancy is recorded and not resolved: 1508.07161 attributes 'T_c = 159.5 +/- 1.5 GeV' to its ref.[20], where 1404.3565v1 prints 159 +/- 1. It affects only the tree's refusal bound at 159.0. Nothing here is WRONG.

To DATA-DEPENDENT or WRONG: a later SM lattice determination of Gamma(T) at the physical Higgs mass, beyond leading log or in the continuum limit, that moves ln Gamma by more than the stated 1.9 or puts T* outside 131.7 +/- 2.3. audits.published_statement: Abstract: 'We use the observed time delay of (+1.74 +/- 0.05) s between GRB 170817A and GW170817 to: (i) constrain the difference between the speed of gravity and the speed of light to be between -3e-15 and +7e-16 times the speed of light'. Sec 4.1: 'the fractional speed difference during the trip can be written Delta v/v_EM ~ v_EM Delta t / D, where Delta v = v_GW - v_EM ... we conservatively use here D = 26 Mpc, the lower bound of the 90% credible interval on luminosity distance derived from the GW signal ... If we conservatively assume that the peak of the GW signal and the first photons were emitted simultaneously, attributing the entire (+1.74 +/- 0.05) s lag to faster travel by the GW signal, this time difference provides an upper bound on Delta v. To obtain a lower bound ... we assume the SGRB signal was emitted 10 s after the GW signal. The resulting constraint ... -3e-15 <= Delta v/v_EM <= +7e-16 (1)'. The same section continues: '... emission of photons before the merger is also possible (Tsang et al. 2012). Hence, certain exotic scenarios can extend this time difference window to (-100 s, 1000 s), yielding a 2 orders of magnitude broadening of the allowed velocity range on either side. While the emission times of the two messengers are inherently model dependent...'
published_hypotheses: H1 distance: D = 26 Mpc, the lower end of the 90% credible interval on the GW luminosity distance. A smaller D gives a weaker bound, so this choice is conservative.

H2 emission ordering (upper bound): the GW peak and the first photons were emitted simultaneously, so no photons left before the GW peak. The source itself says pre-merger photon emission is possible, and names an exotic window (-100 s, 1000 s).
H3 emission lag (lower bound): the SGRB was emitted no more than 10 s after the GW.
H4 the bound is on v_GW relative to v_EM (the photon speed), and dispersion of the gamma rays by the intergalactic medium is taken as negligible.
H5 background gravitational potentials affect both messengers in the same way (the Shapiro difference is treated separately in sec 4.3).
H6 the travel-time difference is small, the fractional speed difference is constant over the trip, and luminosity distance serves as the travel distance.
H7 one event and one line of sight (NGC 4993). The source says future joint detections are needed to separate emission delay from propagation delay.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS. (A) Recomputed from the source's own inputs, the upper bound is +6.6888e-16, published as +7e-16 (rounded up, the conservative direction). The lower bound is -3.1053e-15, published as -3e-15. That is rounded down by about 3.5%: a rounding discrepancy, recorded, not a refutation, and the tree does not use that side. (D) The source's exotic window gives -3.73e-13 to +3.80e-14, factors of 121 and 57, which reproduces the source's '2 orders of magnitude'. (E) The tree's arithmetic at 50 digits reproduces branelink.py:61-66 to every printed digit: beta = 3.741657386774e-8, 1/beta = 26726124.1912, T = 134009348.4 s, Delta_tau = 93.80654388 ns. The identity sqrt(1-1/(1+d)^2) = sqrt(d(2+d))/(1+d) is proved symbolically. With the unrounded 6.689e-16 the saving would be 89.64 ns. audits.published_statement:
Abstract: 'in dimensions >= 3 causally compact topology-changing spacetimes cannot satisfy Einstein's equation (with a reasonable source); i.e., there are severe dynamical obstructions to topology change. This result extends a previous one due to Tipler. Like Tipler's result, it makes no assumptions about geodesic completeness'.

Theorem 3: 'Let M be a (time-oriented) causally compact interpolating spacetime of dimension >= 3 with initial surface S1 and final surface S2. Suppose that i) every full ... null geodesic has a point on it at which F_abcd = U_[a R_b]ef[c U_d] U^e U^f != 0 ...; and ii) for any point u0 on a past-complete, affinely parametrized null geodesic lambda(u), the half-integral null convergence condition ... holds along lambda to the past of u0. Then M is diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1], and S1 and S2 are connected.'

Sec. V: the curvature restrictions 'mainly follow from reasonable restrictions on the source'.

Sec. VI: for quantum fields, integral conditions 'might perhaps hold. This is so far only a piece of wishful thinking.'

Sec. IX.B: 'there might be violations of the energy conditions large enough to allow assumption (ii) to be violated. Some discussions of wormhole creation are ... based precisely on large violations of the energy condition'. Also in IX.B, weakening the curvature constraints 'would not affect the presence of causality violations'.
published_hypotheses: H1: a smooth, non-degenerate Lorentz metric on a smooth, Hausdorff, paracompact manifold. Sec. VIII (C^0 metrics) and Sec. IX.C (degenerate metrics) name these cases as outside.
H2: time-oriented.
H3: M is a connected interpolating spacetime between disjoint spacelike S1 (initial) and S2 (final), with an optional compact timelike tube T diffeomorphic to dS1 x [0,1].
H4: causally compact, i.e. the closure of I(p) is compact for every p.
H5: dimension n >= 3 (the focusing lemma is stated for n > 2).
H6 (i): the null generic condition on every FULL null geodesic. This is weaker than Tipler's version.
H7 (ii): the half-integral null convergence condition along every past-complete affinely parametrised null geodesic.

H8 (only for reading the theorem): Einstein's equation, with Lambda allowed, serves only to turn a source restriction into (i)/(ii). 'Reasonable source' means a T_ab that yields (i) and (ii). The theorem itself is about curvature.
No geodesic-completeness assumption.

audits.lacked_data:
Theorem 3 uses no measured datum. The one constant it touches, Lambda, was unmeasured in 1994 and is measured now, and it drops out identically (D2). What Borde lacked, by his own account, was knowledge of how quantum sources behave on average: he calls (ii) for quantum fields 'wishful thinking'.

Later work points both ways.
(a) Several results show that making or holding a throat needs a source that violates integrated null convergence: D6 for every static zero-redshift throat, 2505.02210 for an explicit nucleation, and FSW. That confirms the theorem's logic: no counterexample satisfying (i)-(ii) exists, and the escapes sit where Borde placed them.
(b) Quantum-inequality work, read here only via restatement, suggests half-line integrated conditions can fail for quantum fields. That narrows how often the theorem applies to a semiclassical source. It does not falsify the theorem, and it was not shown here that (ii) itself fails.

No missing datum makes the theorem wrong. The open question is whether real sources meet its hypothesis. This does not favour M either: where (ii) fails, IX.B and Theorem 1 keep the CTC price under causal compactness.

audits.published_statement: The textbook statement (NAMED-NOT-READ): a point magnetic dipole m in vacuum has the field B(r) = (mu0/4pi)[3(m.rhat)rhat - m]/r^3 for r != 0. This is the leading term of the exterior multipole expansion, and an l-pole falls as r^-(l+2). Restated by use: 1309.4167 sec 2.2 'the surface dipolar magnetic field strength B, defined as B = 3.2 x 10^19 (P Pdot)^1/2 G ... Note that the expression for B assumes simple vacuum dipole radiation and ignores the potentially important torques due to magnetospheric variability and the internal superfluid'; 2405.15484 eq (1): Omega_dot_vac = -(2R^6/3Ic^3) B^2 sin^2 chi Omega^3, with 'B is the surface magnetic field at the dipole cap'; 1308.4987 p.1: '(under the assumption of rotating magnetic dipole in vacuo) ... B = 6 x 10^12 G at the magnetic equator'.
published_hypotheses: H1 VACUUM / CURRENT-FREE outside the source: curl B = 0 in the region considered. 1309.4167 sec 2.2 says 'vacuum dipole' and 1308.4987 p.1 says 'dipole in vacuo'.

H2 QUASI-STATIC NEAR ZONE: r << R_L = c/Omega = cP/2pi. Beyond the light cylinder the field lines open and the field is not dipolar. 2405.15484 eq (19) names R_L; the 1/r far-zone behaviour is textbook, NAMED-NOT-READ.
H3 LEADING MULTIPOLE: the dipole term dominates. Higher l-poles fall as r^-(l+2) (derived here), so a surface field that includes multipoles is not the dipole amplitude (1308.4987, SGR 0418+5729).
H4 FIXED ANGLE: B(r) = B(R)(R/r)^3 holds along a fixed direction, and the pole field is 2 x the equatorial field. The catalogued B is the EQUATORIAL value for R = 10 km and I = 1e45 g cm^2.
H5 The magnetar's B is INFERRED from P and Pdot under H1 (spin-down); it is not measured at the surface (1309.4167 sec 2.2).

(1) The tree applies the result to a linearised metric that is Ricci-flat only at O(M). The tree names this (composite.py:102-104, 326-327). On a correct null screen that metric's trace is 8.69e-3 of the maximum component at the static point, not 'four digits' (composite.py:43-44).

audits.published_statement: Abstract (p.1): 'We find in all cases studied that the energy density fluctuations are large whenever the local energy density is negative. This is taken to mean that the gravitational field of a system with negative energy density, such as the Casimir vacuum, is not described by a fixed classical metric but is undergoing large metric fluctuations.' Sec. III.B (p.9): 'Our primary concern is whether or not Delta << 1, which is best determined by numerical evaluation of Delta using Eqs. (3.2), (3.18), and (3.19). The figures illustrate the results. For states which are sufficiently close to coherent states, i.e. r << |alpha|, we do indeed find that Delta << 1. However, as the magnitude of the squeeze parameter r increases relative to that of |alpha|, we find that Delta increases. By the point that the state is sufficiently squeezed to have rho = <:T00:> < 0, we always have that Delta is at least of order unity. Thus squeezed states for which the energy density is negative exhibit large energy density fluctuations.' Fig. 2 caption: '...gamma = delta = 0 and theta = pi/2... Delta << 1 only when s >> r, the region of classical behavior. Otherwise, Delta ~ 1.' Sec. III.A (p.6): 'cos(2theta) > sqrt2 eps. In this case we have Delta(x) > 1.' Sec. III.C (p.12): 'Delta' >= 1/2, Delta >= 1/3 ... the dimensionless Casimir energy density fluctuations are always at least of order unity.' Sec. V (p.16): 'states of a quantized field in which the mean energy density is negative seem to exhibit large energy density fluctuations. This was illustrated in our model calculations for squeezed states and for the Casimir vacuum state.'
published_hypotheses: H1: a massless, minimally coupled scalar field in FLAT spacetime, in a box of side L with periodic boundary conditions (2.1)-(2.6).

H2: the measure is KF (3.2), Delta(x) = |(<:T00^2:> - <:T00:>^2)/<:T00^2:>|. It is taken in the coincidence limit, for the 00 component, with every operator normal-ordered against the Minkowski vacuum, the quartic one included. It is a POINTWISE measure.

H3: the 'cases studied' are four. (i) The vacuum+2 superposition (2.15). (ii) The squeezed COHERENT family D(alpha)S(zeta)|0> of (3.9)-(3.19). (iii) The squeezed vacuum, which is the alpha=0 limit (3.22)-(3.23). (iv) The Casimir vacuum with periodic z (3.24)-(3.45).

audits.published_statement: Abstract: 'We establish the dynamical instability of a static, spherically symmetric, and infinitesimally thin shell in general relativity. The shell is made up of a perfect fluid with a barotropic equation of state, and it produces a Schwarzschild spacetime in its exterior and a Minkowski spacetime in its interior. ... We reveal the existence of two modes with a purely imaginary frequency, one negative ..., the other positive (which describes an exponential growth); these modes occur for all sampled values of the shell's compactness and adiabatic index, and all sampled values of the multipolar order l >= 2, in the even-parity sector of the perturbation. ... we show that a Newtonian shell also is necessarily unstable to a time-dependent perturbation. Our conclusion suggests that a compact object that features a thin shell at its surface will be dynamically unstable.' Sec I D (p.4): 'An unstable mode exists also for l = 3 ... and for all other values of l that we could sample in our numerical exploration.' Sec VII A (p.23): l = 4 also computed. Fig. 1 (p.3), l = 2 only: Im{omega (R^3/M)^{1/2}} against M/R in [0, 0.30] at Gamma = 2 (axis 0.52-0.66), and against Gamma in [1.8, 2.4] at M/R = 0.2 (axis 0.56-0.64). Sec X H (p.41): 'The dynamical instability for any multipole order l takes its origin in the existence of a normal mode of vibration with a negative eigenvalue'; for l = 0, lambda = Gamma - 3/2; for l = 1, lambda_+ = (3 Gamma - 4)/2 and lambda_- = 0, the translation.

audits.lacked_data: PSP's conclusion rests on no measured datum. It is a linear-stability computation within a stated model, so no later measurement can move it. What they lacked was coverage: in GR they sampled l = 2-4, M/R <= 0.3 and Gamma in [1.8, 2.4]. Evidence FOR: the Newtonian derivation here, which reproduces four printed formulas exactly, closes that gap in the Newtonian limit. A growing mode exists for every Gamma > 0 and every l >= 2 (z3 unsat), and it grows faster with l, so more coverage strengthens the instability. Evidence AGAINST the tree's extension: the model has no shear or bending rigidity, no finite thickness, no collisionless (Vlasov) or anisotropic matter, and no non-vacuum surroundings. PSP do not claim these, the tree's own matter models fall there, and Le 2606.22531v4 says so. Pani et al.'s de Sitter-interior null result is an unresolved counter-indication for interior-independence. Net: no datum moves PSP's statement; the tree's use needs hypotheses PSP do not supply.
audits.grade_evidence: (1) The published statement STANDS as published. I read it at source (cached alphaXiv text, md5 9916ebc7...). An independent Newtonian derivation reproduces Eqs (10.52b), (10.54) and (10.57) and the l = 0 eigenvalue exactly, and proves (z3 unsat) the Newtonian instability for all Gamma > 0 and l >= 2. (2) The tree's use is broader than the source in four named ways: (a) 'all compactness, all Gamma' where the source has 'all sampled' (GR: M/R <= 0.3, Gamma in [1.8, 2.4]), stability.py:81-83 and obstruct.py:120-121; (b) M_in >= 0 where the source computes M_in = 0 and calls interior-independence a contested belief, stability.py:83-84; (c) the barotropic perfect-fluid hypothesis is dropped in 'not escapable while self-gravitating', wall.py:186-187 and obstruct.py:119-127, although the tree's own matter models are outside it (Le 2606.22531v4 restates PSP with exactly this restriction); (d) 'beta^2 does not appear in the unstable branch at all' (wall.py:128, 455-456) holds for the mode's existence but not its rate, since kappa_2 falls from 0.627 to 0.346 as Gamma goes from 1.5 to infinity. (3) The l = 2 coefficient 0.6 is applied to all l >= 2 (wall.py:440, 454-469), while the re-derived rates grow as ~l/2. The tree's density-ceiling numbers therefore understate the constraint, which strengthens rather than weakens its withdrawal of the diffuse corner. Nothing is WRONG: no counterexample within PSP's hypotheses exists or is claimed.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: -> STANDS for the tree's use: a result that the l >= 2 growing mode persists for shells with shear or bending rigidity, finite thickness, or collisionless/anisotropic matter, plus relativistic coverage for all M/R < 1/2 and all Gamma (or the tree narrowing its wording to 'sampled' and 'barotropic perfect fluid'). -> DATA-DEPENDENT: if the density ceiling were re-expressed with an l_max set by a physical thickness or rigidity, the conclusion would move with that material datum. -> WRONG: only a computed barotropic perfect-fluid thin shell (Minkowski/Schwarzschild, l >= 2) with no growing mode, which the z3 result excludes in the Newtonian limit. -> Reading pp. 5, 8, 10-22 and 24-40 (Secs IV-VII, X D-F) would check the Newtonian lambda_+- derived here against the printed ones and give the relativistic l = 3 and 4 rates, without changing the drift findings.

(iii) Lobo arXiv:0710.4474 eq (70); the shell's Lanczos sigma and P are eqs (115)-(122). (iv) Le arXiv:2602.18023v6, eq (17) and sec. 2.5 (the DEC slack min_i(rho - |p_i|)).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries. In this pass (2026-10-02) I re-read 1810.02487v5 and 2306.07326v3 at source and quote them verbatim. Prop. 5: 'DEC for type I is equivalent to rho >= 0 and rho^2 >= p_i^2 ..., which is equivalent to rho >= 0 and rho >= |p_i|'. Eq (2.8): 'DEC : rho - p_i >= 0 ... in addition to WEC'. 1810.02487 p.3 adds: 'the proofs ... are absent in Ref. [7]'. 0710.4474, gr-qc/9506083 and 2602.18023 were read in the earlier pass of this docket.

audits.published_statement: Maeda-Martinez 1810.02487 Prop. 5: for a Type I T^(a)(b) = diag(rho, p_1, ..., p_{n-1}) in n >= 3 dimensions, 'DEC for type I is equivalent to rho >= 0 and rho^2 >= p_i^2, which is equivalent to rho >= 0 and rho >= |p_i|'. In observer form (eq 3.16), J.J <= 0 is equivalent to (1 - sum a_i^2) rho^2 + sum a_i^2 (rho^2 - p_i^2) >= 0 for every timelike observer. Maeda 2306.07326 eq (2.8) gives the same condition as 'rho - p_i >= 0 in addition to WEC', where WEC = rho >= 0 and rho + p_i >= 0.
published_hypotheses: The stress-energy is Hawking-Ellis Type I, in canonical form diag(rho, p_i) (1810.02487 eq 3.7).
n >= 3. The shell worldvolume has n = 3; the 4D distributional tensor diag(sigma, p, p, 0) gives the same DEC.
The DEC quantifies over all timelike observers (Hawking-Ellis definition). The equivalence is pointwise and algebraic.
No sign is assumed for p_i. The published form is rho >= |p_i|; reducing it to rho - p_i >= 0 needs p_i >= 0, or rho + p_i >= 0 separately (in 2306.07326 eq 2.8 the WEC clause supplies that).
hypothesis_drift: NONE at the definition itself (wall.py:258-260). It names both hypotheses the reduction needs, Type I and p > 0. z3 A2 proves DEC <=> sigma - p >= 0 under them, and the vacuity guard A3 passes.
IMPLICIT and satisfied: isotropy p_theta = p_phi. statics() is the spherically symmetric Lanczos shell, and C1 matches Lobo eqs 121-122.

IMPLICIT and satisfied: every static use stays inside p > 0. p_0 = (1-s)^2/(16 pi R s) > 0 on all of (0,1) (C2). This covers dec_margin (wall.py:258), dec_margin_scaled (:264) and the window 'surface dec iff x < 24/25' (wall.py:47, 243, 517, 554).

DROPPED: p > 0, at wall.py:205-216 (BONUS) and wall.py:377-381 (dec_asymptotic_margin). Along the linear-EOS orbit, p tends to (p_0 - beta^2 sigma_0)/(1+beta^2). That limit is negative in exactly the regime the tree calls 'basin unbounded'. For the tree's own selftest walls (wall.py:584), p crosses zero at R/R0 = 1.0514 (0.3, 0.5), 1.1462 (0.3, 0.2), 1.1165 (0.5, 0.5) and 1.1097 (2/3, 0.9), all computed. Past that radius sigma - p is not the DEC margin; sigma + p is the binding term. z3 A4b gives a counterexample to reading sigma - p without the hypothesis: sigma = 1, p = -2.

CONSEQUENCE, computed: the BOOLEAN conclusion survives. sigma + p = (sigma_0 + p_0)(R/R0)^(-2(1+beta^2)) > 0 exactly (D2), so by z3 D8 the DEC holds iff sigma - p >= 0. 'ANY STRICTLY STABLE WALL AUTOMATICALLY HAS AN UNBOUNDED DOMINANT-ENERGY BASIN' (wall.py:215) is therefore true within the linear-EOS model. The tree never states the sigma + p > 0 fact this depends on. The QUANTITATIVE label does not survive. 'The margin tends to 2(beta^2 sigma_0 - p_0)/(1+beta^2)' (wall.py:207-208) is the limit of sigma - p, but the true DEC margin min(sigma - p, sigma + p) tends to 0+ (sigma_inf + p_inf = 0, D4). At R = 1e6 R0: sigma - p = 7.82e-3, while sigma - |p| = 1.4e-20 (D7). The DEC is asymptotically saturated.

MINOR: 'd(sigma-p)/dR = (1-beta^2) sigma' < 0' (wall.py:206) is an exact identity (D9). The '< 0' also needs beta^2 < 1, which the site does not state. The file treats beta^2 <= 1 as its causality proxy (wall.py:200-202).

WORDING: by eq (3.16), the infimum of the observer flux quantity is (sigma - p)(sigma + p), and no finite observer attains it (A5, A7). The null-pair extremes are {sigma - p, sigma + p} (A6). So sigma - p is the sign-carrying factor; its size is a normalisation convention, not a unique 'worst observer' value. Not grade-moving.

source.located: The owner cites no source: address.py:45-52 and 844-850 state the formula bare. It is the standard leading-order nuclear-size correction, first-order perturbation theory with |psi_nS(0)|^2 <r^2>, and has no single originating paper. It was READ at two sources. (i) Eides, Grotch, Shelyuto, 'Theory of Light Hydrogenlike Atoms', hep-ph/0002158v2 (2000; Phys. Rept. 342, 63 (2001)): Sec. XVII eq (156)-(158) p.98, eq (162)-(164) p.100, Sec. XIX eq (185)-(192) pp.110-111, Table X p.114. (ii) CODATA 2022, arXiv:2409.03787v1: Sec. IV.A.7 eq (49)-(56), eq (30), Table II (r_p,ref 0.8414 fm), Table XXXIII (r_p = 8.4075(64)e-16 m, a_0 = 5.29177210544(82)e-11 m).
source.via: Eides et al. was read live through alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries(hep-ph/0002158), which returned pages 1, 4, 22-23, 98-100, 108-112, 114, 133, 190 and 208. Every Eides quotation in the report was checked again against that page text this stage. CODATA 2022 was read from the full text cached in this workflow (d67/src/casmag/all/2409.03787v1.txt, md5 cc640485b0d9f0fe202f38989dac6a2b): eq (50) at lines 2070-2093 and Table XXXIII r_p at line 5773. Hagelstein-Pascalutsa arXiv:1502.03721 was read live by the earlier pass of this stage. The classics Friar 1979 and Borisoglebsky-Trofimenko 1979 are NAMED-NOT-READ; Eides Table X restates them.

audits.published_statement: Eides-Grotch-Shelyuto hep-ph/0002158 eq (158), verbatim: 'Delta E = (2 pi (Z alpha)/3) <r^2> |psi(0)|^2 = (2 (Z alpha)^4/3 n^3) m_r^3 <r^2> delta_l0'. Here <r^2> comes from the form-factor slope (eq 156) and, for the proton, from the Sachs G_E slope (eq 162-164). p.99: 'shifts the energy level upwards, and is nonvanishing only for the S states'. The derivation (eq 186) assumes 'the size of the nuclear charge distribution is much smaller than the atomic scale', and eq (192) shifts P1/2 at (Z alpha)^6. CODATA 2022 eq (50): 'E(4)_nucl = (2/3) m_e c^2 (Z alpha)^4/n^3 (m_r/m_e)^3 (r_N/lambda_C)^2 delta_l0 ... solely due to the finite rms charge radius r_N of nucleus N.' Both reduce to (4/3) Z^4 (m_r/m_e)^3 (r_N/a_0)^2/n^3 R_inf hc.
published_hypotheses: r_N is the rms charge radius, defined by the slope of the charge form factor (Sachs G_E for the proton). No shape model is assumed: at this order the shift depends on the distribution only through <r^2>, and the first shape dependence appears at (Z alpha)^6 (Eides eq 189, p.111).
The nuclear size is much smaller than the atomic scale (Eides eq 185-186). Hagelstein-Pascalutsa 1502.03721 sharpen this: the form factor must be smooth at Q ~ Z alpha m_r.
Leading order in Z alpha only. The Friar (Z alpha)^5 term, the radiative alpha(Z alpha)^5 terms and the (Z alpha)^6 terms are separate (CODATA eq 49, 51, 56; Eides eq 188-195).
delta_l0: only S states shift at this order; P1/2 shifts at (Z alpha)^6 (Eides eq 192).
Finite nuclear mass enters through the factor m_r^3, i.e. (m_r/m_e)^3.
Hydrogenlike atom with nuclear charge Z.

audits.published_statement: Penrose 1979, quoted word for word by Stoica (1203.3382 pp. 1-2). Page 614: 'In terms of spacetime curvature, the absence of clumping corresponds, very roughly, to the absence of Weyl conformal curvature (since absence of clumping implies spatial-isotropy, and hence no gravitational principal null-directions).' Page 630: 'this restriction on the early geometry should be something like: the Weyl curvature C_abcd vanishes at any initial singularity.' Gregoris-Ong-Wang paraphrase it (2004.10222 p. 2): 'near the past singularity (the Big Bang) the Weyl curvature must vanish, and then it started to rise monotonically thereafter as matter starts clumping ... If there is a crunch, future singularity can be arbitrarily distorted and so has large Weyl curvature, unlike the initial singularity.' Stoica's abstract describes Penrose 'conjecturing the vanishing of the Weyl tensor at the Big-Bang singularity'.
published_hypotheses: P1 (Penrose p. 630, via Stoica): the constraint applies only to INITIAL singularities ('at any initial singularity'). Final singularities are left unconstrained (2004.10222 p. 2). The time-asymmetry is put in as a boundary condition, not derived.
P2 (Penrose p. 630): Penrose hedges the form himself with 'something like'. It is a conjecture; Stoica's word is 'conjecturing'.
P3 (Penrose p. 614): the link between clumping and Weyl curvature holds 'very roughly'. It is argued from isotropy and the absence of principal null directions, and no entropy functional is given.

P4 (the literature, not Penrose): gravitational entropy has no agreed definition. CET p. 1: 'a well-motivated and universally agreeable analogue has yet to be found'. 2004.10222 p. 11: 'there is no agreement on a commonly accepted definition of gravitational entropy in cosmology'.

P5 (CET p. 3): the plain measure C^2 'has been argued to fail at isotropic singularities, and also fails to handle the decaying and growing perturbation modes [Rothman-Anninos 1997]'. The ratio C^2/R_abR^ab gives the wrong sense of time for a radiating source [Bonnor 1987] and diverges in vacuum.

P6 (CET pp. 13-16): the CET measure rises with structure formation only under its stated assumptions. These are pure Coulomb-like (Petrov type D) or pure wave-like (type N) fields, linear scalar perturbations of flat RW in longitudinal gauge, a comoving domain, the semi-classical temperature T = |H|/2pi, and u~ decaying more slowly than a^-3. CET also conjectures that a time-symmetric recollapse will be 'problematic for any sensible definition of gravitational entropy'.

Penrose's own hedges ('very roughly', 'something like') and the status 'conjecture' are gone.

SCOPE CHANGED (permute.py:88, 441, 543): the source constrains the initial singularity. The tree says 'the early universe'. The tree's version, a near-FLRW early state, is a weaker claim and better supported. The drift is in attribution: the tree's sentence is not Penrose's hypothesis.

HYPOTHESIS ADDED (permute.py:88-89): 'extremely low GRAVITATIONAL entropy -- Weyl curvature near zero' treats gravitational entropy and Weyl curvature as the same thing without naming a measure. Penrose links Weyl curvature to the absence of clumping only 'very roughly', and no accepted definition of gravitational entropy exists.

REGIME/MEASURE DROPPED (permute.py:89-90, 544): the tree states 'clumping raises it' with no conditions. It fails for the Weyl magnitude in the class studied by 2004.10222, and for P in Bonnor's collapsing sphere (2512.02238).
